author: jochembrouwer
content:
Hi <@316280621783580673>, regarding [PFI/CFI EIP-7907 for Hegotá](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2234#issuecomment-5893875075), I think we should either update that EIP or fork the EIP to a new one. What you likely want to propose is to Meter Contract Code Size, but not increase limit.

I also believe for this one we should really check how necessary this is *now* or for future if we want to keep increasing code size. Cold account load cost should absorb some of the JUMPDEST analysis cost. 
I also want to see if clients store JUMPDEST analysis on disk. For valid JUMPDEST this could be written as bitlist, so would need 256 bytes extra storage for the 64 KiB contract and could be loaded alongside code.
Because BALs declare which accounts are read, we should also see how much more we can optimize there, for instance doingJUMPDEST analysis in prefetcher.
I do want to signal there is this obvious cost, linearly scaling with code size, for the analysis. I do think we need to know if this is the code size (64 KiB) to already charge this cost based on code size, or if this is sufficiently absorbed by current flat load costs (cold account load, per [EIP-8038](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8038#parameters) `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS` cost of `3000`

CC <@968526635735326741> since this essentially "reprices" code load cost by adding costs based on code size (with nonzero cost > 24 KiB code)
